Each prompt's blueprint (the note on the Task completion page) is the target. The response under it is built only from your any-topic cards: card sentences, or a card's drilled part, in the blueprint's order, with no word added or changed and the blanks left as they are. Every move the blueprint has you say is graded: full your cards say it, with its content and shade, once the blanks are filled from this ad; partial they do the job but lose part of it (dotted underline); gap no card says it, and the card that would is written in its place. One subagent per prompt; an independent reviewer then re-checked every full grade.

A move is one piece of content you say (one question, one fact about you, one step of an argument, one item of the recap), not a turn: one turn usually carries several. Main-line moves are the call or conversation as you'd follow it; branches are alternatives said only if an answer goes that way; push-further moves are optional extras.

Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 49 full grades and kept 40; 9 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry most of this call: the opening, quoting the ad's own words back ('a series of mini-flights', 'exceptional rates'), length, the price and what it includes, insurance, the deposit, the evening-before-or-morning-of weather call, the rescheduling window, health paperwork, meeting point, kit, students per instructor, the follow-on course, and most push asks. They break in four places: the body (nothing states your weight or fitness, or asks weight and age limits), the mechanics of a first flight (alone or attached, how high, how many, the radio, getting back up the slope), anything sent in writing (confirmation, meeting point, the weather text), and the recap, where no card says 'so that's X, Y and Z'.

How it was pushed
  • QB051 quotes the ad back twice, «une série de mini-vols» and «tarifs exceptionnels», so the staff member defines both vague phrases in their own words.
  • QB121's fixed 'à la suite d'un vol' (after a theft) reads as 'after a flight' here; with 'an X-ray' and 'ankle' it asks what insurance covers your own injury.
  • QB081's second [cours] holds 'instructor': 'Vous accueillez combien de personnes par moniteur ?' gives the student-to-instructor ratio.
  • QB080::QN19 does double duty: medical certificate or signed health declaration (adult), and a parent required or a signed parental consent form (teenager).
  • QB084::Q110 ('le matin même, ou la veille au soir ?') is word for word the weather-call timing question.
  • QB173 with 'the cancelled date' ('ces modifications après la date annulée') asks how long the rescheduling credit lasts.
  • QB029::QG007 ('Les exercices au sol seraient quand même maintenus ?') + QB156::QG005 build the insider question: ground work despite the wind, flights made up later.
  • QB138 (flights at higher altitude, tandem flights for example) asks for the clouds the headline sells, and opens the view-seeker's call.
  • QB161 with 'old injury' and 'back or ankle' carries both of the blueprint's examples.
  • QB012::Q212 times both one mini-flight and the walk back up.
  • CB049::C077 + QB044 ('les essais pratiques ... Vous pourriez me les décrire ?') make them describe the ad's vaguest line.
  • QB153 asks what you fly over: a small training slope or a real mountainside.
  • QB089 with 'the rest of the training' asks the next step toward flying higher.
  • QB017's [activité] slot holds the kit list: wings, seats, helmets and radios.
  • QB016 + QB016::Q021 ('pour un participant') get the exact amount and make it per person.
  • CB018::C025 and QB076 take 'one' in a plural slot: 'un ami(s)' and 'un ami venai(en)t' sound the same, so one friend works in speech.
  • CB048::C076 lists what the cover pays: medical costs, mountain rescue, transport to hospital.

Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 31 full grades and kept 24; 7 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: The cards carry the generic spine of this call well: the opening, being a beginner, the weekday-evening window, start dates, what 'flexible schedules' means, registration fee, themed-evening frequency, address, shoes and booking, and slot cards stretch further than expected (own song for a wedding, open practice hours, costume fees). They break where this blueprint is most specific. Nothing covers partner dancing (bring a partner, rotation, role balance, waiting lists), nothing says 'I'd come alone', nothing asks how far a running term has got, and almost nothing asks the school to do something for you (hold a place, email, call back, tell the teacher). The recap is mostly unsayable.

21% of 89 moves fully carried by your cards · 19 full · 47 partial · 23 gaps
main line 17/58 full · branches 0/19 full · push further 2/12 full
Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 30 full grades and kept 19; 11 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the finding-out half of this call well: the opening, tour times and length, what is inside, the workshop's places, length, price, minimum numbers and take-home, the age check for the climb, the weather questions, the dining questions, parking, the walk and what to bring, often on the ad's own words. They break where the call stops asking and starts acting or reading back: giving a booking name, the waiting list and call-back, a labelled read-back, the text confirmation, holding places. The deck also has nothing for splitting or minding siblings, steps, re-entry or cards. Most partials lose the date, the four of you, or the exact item.

How it was pushed
  • Tour included in the entry: CB086 with 'the entry ticket' and 'guide' asks whether the ticket also includes a guide on site.
  • Children's ages: CB051 ('I've got a [thing] and a [thing]') filled with a child of ten and a child of seven.
  • Does it run with only two: Section B's drilled part BAY283 (no 'tu') plus QB029::QG007, 'maybe only two will take part; would the workshops still go ahead?'.
  • Take-home the same day: QB160, the pickup-delay card, filled with finishing the workshop and the children's creation.
  • Ill that morning: QB161 with 'one of the children' and 'a sudden illness'.
  • Can a 7-year-old go up: QB018 with 'under eight' so the question covers her exactly.
  • When the view is clearest: QB045 with 'these landscapes', the ad's mountains and rivers.
  • Children's menu: QB060 'are there children's menus as well?'.
  • Picnic allowed: QB020 with 'repas tirés du sac' (packed lunches); where to eat it: QB138 with picnic areas at the castle.
  • GPS: QB123 asks the exact address of the castle entrance, which also meets the service-gate risk.
  • Walk from the car park: QB012::Q212 with 'le trajet à pied' instead of CB072, which would be heard as the drive.
  • What to wear and bring: QB109 'special clothing for this kind of session' plus QB023 'examples of things to bring for the workshop'.
  • Family or combined ticket: QB126::Q173 with a family or combined ticket against separate tickets.
  • Birthday session: CB054's drilled part, CB018::C141 (my son and a few of his friends) and QB003 (book as a group).

Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 27 full grades and kept 19; 8 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the logistics spine of this call: days, frequency, meeting point, set-off time, the ad's word 'gentle', length, kit and cash, entry fees, rain, membership cost and contents, medical certificate, booking a place, and half the recap. They break in three places. The opening: no card says who Min is (new here, weekday job, no car) or asks whether a non-member can come once, the gate question of the whole call. Walking-club mechanics: car-sharing, pace, climbing, cancellations, finishing point. The close: no slot card to say back a place or a name and number, give an email, or have the leader told a newcomer is coming. Partials mostly ask the right thing one notch too generally.

How it was pushed
  • Car-share contribution: QB085 (is it customary to leave a [contribution] to [the driver]) plus QB105::Q139 (how much is the [contribution] for the [petrol]).
  • Kit and cash: QB137's drilled part holds the blueprint's list as one fill; QB035 ('and if so, what kind of fees?') then asks what the cash is for.
  • 'Gentle': QB051 quotes the ad's own word back ('what exactly do you mean by gentle hikes?').
  • Recap distance: CB024::C056 '[length], ça me va' holds the kilometres, said back and accepted.
  • Recap date and set-off time: CB010::C014 'D'accord… [date] et [date]' echoes both in one line.
  • Recap 'nothing to pay': the drilled part of BAY214::BP0983 from bank B, which has no tu ('from what I gather, it's completely free').
  • Rain: QB029 (what is planned in case of [rain]) plus QB029::QG007 (would [the walks] still go ahead?).
  • Medical certificate: QB080::QN19 (is a [medical certificate] required to [join], or is a signed [waiver] enough?).
  • Membership contents: QB017 asks whether the walks and the insurance are in the joining fee, the item the blueprint names first.
  • Child: QB018 (are children under [age] allowed on [the walks]).
  • Entry fee and when it is paid: QB078::Q108 with 'entry', then QB095::Q203's drilled part ('does it all have to be paid in advance').
  • Seasonal highlight date: QB010 ('when exactly do [those walks] start') reused for the push.

Appelez-nous au 07 98 76 54 32

20% of 113 moves fully carried by your cards · 23 full · 52 partial · 38 gaps
main line 10/46 full · branches 11/43 full · push further 2/24 full
Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 35 full grades and kept 23; 12 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the question spine of this call well: how the price is built, the children's rate, what it includes, drinks, the cake, hours, the deposit, who sets up speakers and decorations. They break in three places. Facts about this party (guests from three to ninety, vegetarians, a house that seats 25) have almost no 'here is my situation' card that fits. The paper end of the call has nothing: no card asks them to hold a date, asks for anything in writing, reads back a recap or says 'I'll send you'. And on the pushes the cards keep the job but drop the scene: a guest tripping on a speaker cable, lifts home, the fuse.

How it was pushed
  • QB083 'Ce serait pour [date], vers [date]. C'est possible de votre côté ?' gives the date and the 'are you free?' in one line.
  • QB012::Q212 with [the hold] ('combien de temps dure l'option') asks how long a pencilled date stays held.
  • QB126 + QB126::Q180 ('Le prix se calcule au [couvert] ?') + QB126::Q173 ([forfait] / [each service separately]) rebuild 'per head, a package, or item by item'.
  • QB037::Q215 does two jobs: [package]/[content] asks 'your packages or our brief?', and [cake]/[cake] asks 'your cake or ours?'.
  • QB028::Q177 'Côté [wine] et [the toast]… ou c'est vous qui fournissez tout ?' asks included-or-bring-our-own, and again for tables, chairs and tableware.
  • QB064::QN57 '[servez] aussi les [invités] âgés qui ont besoin d'un [service à table]' turns an age card into table service for older guests.
  • QB091 'participer à l'[installation] des [enceintes / décorations]' turns 'how involved must we be' into who sets up the speakers and who puts up and takes down the decorations.
  • CB085 ('je dois prévoir [an afternoon] d'[activities] pour mes [young guests], ou c'est vous qui vous en occupez ?') asks whether to hire the children's entertainment yourself.
  • QB109 'une [taille] particulière pour ce genre de [mur de photos]' plus QB048::Q239 'avec combien d'avance' cover the photo format and the deadline.
  • QB078::Q098 'ajouter uniquement l'[heure supplémentaire] à [la formule]' prices the extra hour.
  • CB072 (travel time) answers how far their venue is; QB060 'y a-t-il des [frais de location] en plus ?' asks whether the hire is in their price.
  • CB050::C082 '[Sunday afternoon] et [Saturday evening]… la différence de prix entre les deux' carries the cheaper-slot push in full.
  • QB077::Q097 'ce que j'aurais de plus si je prenais [all four services]' asks for the free extra for booking everything.
  • CB009::C013 drilled part 'j'aimerais prendre [Saturday the 12th]' gets the hold from none to partial; QB033::Q040 does the same for glasses per person.

23% of 84 moves fully carried by your cards · 19 full · 33 partial · 32 gaps
main line 14/48 full · branches 3/27 full · push further 2/9 full
Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 27 full grades and kept 19; 8 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the money and logistics spine of this call: the total, what's included, whether the prescription costs extra, delivery time, signing, customs, the money-back window and when it starts, the frame warranty, coating failure. They break where the call turns on eyes and paperwork. No card states a fact about Min beyond CB051's two slots, so the prescription date, the missing pupillary distance, the current fit, the arm sizes and the work benefits all go unsaid. No card asks for an optician, a callback, an email, or a name, and nothing says a recap back, so the close collapses. Most partials are generic 'what's planned in case of [thing]' cards standing in for a sharp 'who pays, you or me?'.

How it was pushed
  • CB051 'Moi, j'ai un [chose] et un [chose]' carries the prescription itself: a minus 3.5 in both eyes and a 1.25 astigmatism on the right.
  • QB042::Q053's drilled part 'si le [chose] est imposé pour [activité]' asks whether the frame choice is restricted for my prescription, then again for tinted prescription lenses.
  • QB039::Q048 'payer un supplément en fonction de mon [degré de correction]' asks whether the recommended thickness is in the base price.
  • QB051 + QB149 ask what 'satisfied or your money back' means, then 'any prescription lens, not just frames on their own'.
  • QB012::Q212 'combien de temps dure [la période satisfait ou remboursé]' and QB010 'quand commencent exactement [les jours de retour]' give the day count and its start date.
  • QB088's drilled part 'can the order be left at the door' answers 'do I need to sign for it'.
  • QB078::Q108 'les frais de [douane]' asks about customs fees on delivery.
  • QB138 + QB067 ask for partner opticians in my city and whether going to one costs extra.
  • QB132 'si vous utilisez des [verres polarisés] ou d'autres [filtres] pour vos [lunettes de soleil]' asks about polarized lenses neutrally.
  • QB077 'what does the [blue-light] [option] cover that the basic [anti-reflective] doesn't' handles the blue light upsell.
  • QB029::QN18 'si la [couche] se dégradait pendant [la première année]' asks about a coating that peels in year one.
  • CB009's drilled part + QB016::Q210 get the all-in total for a pair with anti-reflective lenses, and CB009::C013 confirms that total in the recap.
  • CB055 'je pense qu'il vaut mieux que je regarde la [collection] et que je choisisse moi-même' stops the frame pitch.

main line 11/57 full · branches 5/17 full · push further 2/17 full
Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 27 full grades and kept 18; 9 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry this call wherever it asks a business something: prices, what a price includes, parts, the loan car's excess, mileage and deposit, the weather, the key at reception. They break in three places. Saying who you are: the Clio, its mileage, the squeal, the scraped bumper, the only car, the work car park; no card states a situation like this. The written channel: no card sends or asks for anything by text or in writing, so the photos, plate, quote, booking reference and confirmation fall out. Setting terms rather than asking: two prices approved in advance, a 100-euro ceiling, 'text me first', most of the recap. Questions survive; arrangements do not.

B-21

VOLUNTEERS FOR SENIORS

blueprint →Volunteering & charity · Volunteering/solidarity
The prompt, English | French
Prompt

You have read this advertisement for an association. You talk about it to a friend who is looking for an activity.

VOLUNTEERS FOR SENIORS

VOLUNTEERS WANTED

The association "Leisure for Seniors" is looking for volunteers of all ages to lead:

reading workshops

computer workshops

gardening activities

card games, chess, scrabble...

Give a little of your time, give joy and join us.

Contact us at 0556768840

Consigne

Vous avez lu cette publicité pour une association. Vous en parlez à un(e) ami(e) qui cherche une activité.

BÉNÉVOLES POUR SENIORS

RECHERCHE BÉNÉVOLES

L'association « Loisirs pour les Seniors » recherche des bénévoles de tout âge pour animer :

des ateliers de lecture

des ateliers d'informatique

des activités de jardinage

des jeux de carte, d'échec, de scrabble...

Donnez un peu de votre temps, donnez de la joie et rejoignez-nous.

Contactez-nous au 0556768840

17% of 109 moves fully carried by your cards · 18 full · 71 partial · 20 gaps
main line 7/50 full · branches 9/43 full · push further 2/16 full
Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 33 full grades and kept 18; 15 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the spine of this blueprint: the opening on the friend's search, the ad as a list before the word volunteer, the association named second, most doubt answers (a hobby not a job, start at the card table, the ad doesn't say so we call, I'll come with you) and, through Section A cards spoken to the association, nearly every question on the call. They break where the blueprint is most specific: the scenes (the scrabble board set for two o'clock, the basil, the great-grandson on the tablet), the timing problem for a friend who works days, the activities that join two lines, and the volunteer checks. Many cards do the job but lose the ad's exact shade.

Pushing it further

L'idée, c'est pas de supprimer les activités qui existent déjà — c'est plutôt que tu débarques et que tu dises : « Hé les gars, on pourrait aussi faire d'autres trucs. » Comme ça, t'as un mélange d'activités de loisir, pour s'amuser, mais aussi des trucs plus sérieux, avec plus d'impact.The idea isn't to get rid of the activities they already have. It's more like you show up and say, "Hey guys, we could do some other stuff too." That way, you've got a mix of leisure stuff, just for fun, but also more serious stuff that has more of an impact.

You could set up a [game] app so they can keep a game going with their grandkids between sessions.

For someone whose eyes have stopped them reading, you could set up [audiobooks] or large text on a tablet.

You could help them send photos of [their plants] to the family.

That way it's not just an hour a week: it's something they use every day.

How it was pushed
  • Call questions from the Section A bank (QB011, QB123::Q168, QB051 + QB125, QB138, QB082::QN22, QB123, QB137): their vous is spoken to the association on the speaker call, never to the friend.
  • CB044 (A bank, no vous) 'I don't think it says in the ad' + BAY486 'you won't know unless you ask' made the when/where branch full.
  • CB049::C077 (A bank, no vous) + BAY480::BP0023 made 'I don't know the reading format, we'll ask on the call' full.
  • BCY020::BP0823 filled twice spells out what 'lead' means: choose texts, read them aloud, run the talk; set out the boards, pair players, run the games.
  • BCY066 drilled part + BAY446::BP1011 ('not a real teacher with pupils in a classroom') carries '"to lead" sounds like a stage'.
  • BAY101 drilled part (decades of experience, you never know what you'll learn by spending time with them) carries being taught by people with fifty years of practice.
  • BAY246 + BCY072::BP0413 answer 'unpaid work' with 'a hobby, not a job: you'd be doing something you already love'.
  • BAY317::BP0446 + BAY317 filled 'play cards' / 'lead' answer 'I'm not a teacher': then don't, start at the card table.
  • BCY021 drilled part 'basically, you become [that workshop's leader]' lands 'that's the one you'd run'.
  • BCY012 with the four lines as the fill gives the opening menu without the word volunteer.
  • BAY223 (club fee vs classes) + BAY481::BP0253 drilled part carry 'no course fee, maybe a membership fee, we'll ask'.
  • BAY484::BP0104 drilled part (find out the place, then decide) answers the care-home doubt.
  • BAY297 + BAY299::BP0317 ('if not the weekend, after work') make the office-hours follow-up full.
  • BAY253 gives the retired friend 'the others would be people like you'; BCY125::BP0512 + BAY266 carry 'we go together, nobody walks in alone'.
  • BCY110::BP0873 ('no idea what they'll say, but it doesn't hurt to ask') carries asking on the call whether they'd welcome a joined activity.

CANOE-CAMPING TRIP

blueprint →Travel & stays · Travel/getaway
The prompt, English | French
Prompt

You have read this travel agency advertisement. You are talking about it to a friend with whom you want to go on vacation.

CANOE-CAMPING TRIP

THE TRAVEL AGENCY VACANCES NATURE IS ORGANIZING A WEEK OF « CANOE-CAMPING »

Paddle by day and sleep comfortably in a tent at night.

Experience moments of calm, but also of challenge and adventure! Discover the most beautiful landscapes of the region and fill up on fresh air!

All reservations possible at: www.vacancesnature.ca

Consigne

Vous avez lu cette publicité d’agence de voyage. Vous en parlez à un(e) ami(e) avec qui vous voulez partir en vacances.

SÉJOUR CANOT CAMPING

L'AGENCE DE VOYAGE VACANCES NATURE ORGANISE UNE SEMAINE EN « CANOT-CAMPING »

Pagayez de jour et dormez confortablement dans une tente le soir.

Vivez des instants de calme, mais aussi de dépassement et d'aventure ! Découvrez les plus beaux paysages de la région et faites le plein d'air pur !

Toutes les réservations possibles sur : www.vacancesnature.ca

Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 13 full grades and kept 7; 6 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the frame of this blueprint: describing the trip, quoting "comfortably", admitting the price isn't in the ad, asking what it covers, proposing to rent a canoe first, and keeping an exit open. They break where the blueprint gets physical and specific to canoes: who sits where and why the boat goes at the friend's pace, the day-one and day-four scenes, the trial's details, portages, bugs by season, swimming, the room for the eighth night, and the exact close (tonight at eight, two places, Saturday rental, Sunday booking). No card checks something together on a website, so the list leans on "call them" cards, which clash with an ad that gives only a website.

  • BAY038 ("in a canoe we'd see the [region] from another angle and reach less-known places") for "shores no road reaches".

  • BCY004 ("T'as déjà pensé à [activité] ?") with "a week of canoe-camping" as the opening question.

The prompt, English | French
Prompt

You have read this advertisement for a theatre workshop. You are telling a friend about it who is looking for a creative activity for their free afternoons.

THEATRE WORKSHOP

We are looking for a participant for a

THEATRE WORKSHOP

- Perform in front of an audience

- Practise different techniques: singing, dancing, etc.

- Develop creativity, listening

- Meet professional actors

Come and create a show!

Further information and registration on our website

www.onimprovise.com

Consigne

Vous avez lu cette publicité pour un atelier de théâtre. Vous en parlez à un(e) ami(e) qui cherche une activité créative pour ses après-midis libres.

ATELIER THÉÂTRE

Nous cherchons participant pour un

ATELIER THÉÂTRE

- Jouer devant un public

- Pratiquer différentes techniques : chant, danse, etc.

- Développer la créativité, l'écoute

- Rencontrer des comédiens professionnels

Venez créer un spectacle !

Renseignement complémentaire et inscription sur notre site

www.onimprovise.com

Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 26 full grades and kept 20; 6 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the logistics and the reassurance, and break on the arguments that make this ad this friend's. Full moves: the offer (a workshop where you act, sing and dance), 'they teach it', 'you won't be alone up there', 'not in the ad', the site checks, and most questions for the message to the group, through Section A cards (costumes, dance shoes, tickets, length, show dates). The gaps: improvised creation (build on your partner, your scene on stage, no script to learn), the afternoons-as-advantage and actors'-free-days arguments, and everything Min adds personally (first night, running lines, meeting after). The bank has no show, rehearsal, stage or afternoon-availability card.

  • BAY285 ('their schedules may not fit what the group needs, yours will') carries the afternoons-as-advantage argument, moves 31-32.
  • BAY107 with creativity/creative answers 'I'm not sure I have ideas' with the ad's own 'develop creativity'.

  • BAY262::BP0641 ('you could learn through the training they offer') turns the ad's 'practise' into 'they teach it'.
  • BCY110::BP0838 drilled part with 'meetings with the actors' plus BAY483::BP0692 gives 'it's vague; the site will say which'.
  • BCY093 drilled part ('you're right, it says they're looking for a new participant') turns the newcomer fear around.
  • BCY110::BP0145 drilled part says the price 'wasn't in the ad' word for word.
  • Section A question cards, addressed to the group in the message (vous is right there): QB028::Q177 for costumes and dance shoes, QB091 for selling tickets, QB017 for costumes, QB010 for when the performances start, QB012::Q212 for how long, QB007::Q181 for prices.
  • BAY497::BP0900 plus BCY111 makes the sit-in a request ('not sure they'd accept, but it could be an option').
  • BAY372 with [sujet] = stage fright asks the group which option suits someone with stage fright: partial for parts fitted to how much each wants to be seen.
  • BAY443::BP0592 plus BAY441 puts the performance at the end, weeks away.

Prompt

You read this job offer in the newspaper. You talk about it to a friend who is looking for work.

THE KEYS TO THE GARDEN

Offer your services on Les Clefs du Jardin.com

We are looking for people to carry out small gardening jobs at private homes:

- Clean and mow the lawns

- Remove the weeds

- Maintain the balconies

- Prune the trees and shrubs

- Water regularly…

Contact us quickly at 0323 43 4334 or on lesclefsdujardin.com

Consigne

Vous avez lu cette offre d’emploi dans le journal. Vous en parlez à un(e) ami(e) qui cherche du travail.

LES CLEFS DU JARDIN

Proposez vos services sur Les Clefs du Jardin.com

Nous recherchons des personnes pour effectuer de petits travaux de jardinage chez des particuliers :

- Nettoyer et tondre les gazons

- Enlever les mauvaises herbes

- Entretenir les balcons

- Tailler les arbres et arbustes

- Arroser régulièrement…

Contactez-nous vite au 0323 43 4334 ou sur lesclefsdujardin.com

They break where the blueprint becomes this ad: 'water regularly' as predictable weekly income, the keys scene and the CV reference, the seasons, the pay arithmetic, the self-employed and benefits questions, insurance, and anything about gardening itself (pruning risk, flats, the walkthrough). Most partials are generic 'ask them about X' or 'you'll meet people' cards that keep the job and drop the specific content. No card holds a scene with a time and a person, or a plan with a time.

How it was pushed
  • BAY316::BP0812 with two verb fills ('Propose juste les trucs dont tu veux bien te charger') carries 'you choose what to offer, so leave out what you can't do'.
  • Drilled hedge of BCY110::BP1198 ('je suis pas sûr à 100 %') before the profile card BCY030::BP0274 keeps the blueprint's 'suggests a platform' shade.
  • BCY110::BP0838 with [winter months] turns an any-topic 'not sure what the [thing] look like, call them' into 'how much in January is a question for the site'.
  • Three cards in a row (BCY097, BAY480::BP0230 drilled, BAY417) give the scam answer: fair worry, contact them to check it's legit, give nothing first.
  • BCY060::BP1148 plus BAY292::BP1190 with [gardening] agrees with 'gardening isn't what I want' without giving up the case.
  • BAY443::BP0592 with [pruning] says 'no pruning yet' exactly.
  • BAY481 with feminine fills ([training], [pay]) makes two of the site checks full.
  • BCY071 then BAY293 make the honest 'it's a bridge, not a salary' line for the friend who needs a full wage.
  • BAY019 with [reference] carries 'it leaves a reference behind'.

6% of 94 moves fully carried by your cards · 6 full · 52 partial · 36 gaps
main line 4/46 full · branches 2/40 full · push further 0/8 full
Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 11 full grades and kept 6; 5 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry 11 of 94 moves fully, 47 in part and 36 not at all. They hold where Min has argued resale before (the sell-to-earn pair, 'I don't pay until I've seen it', a price estimate with a blank) and on generic steering (we look it up together, I'll come with you, keep me posted). They break on what makes this blueprint belong to this ad: the sell-first-then-buy order, the worked numbers ($800, $250, $150, $100), the economics of a private sale (the seller wants it gone, the price moves, no returns), every item-specific check, the seller-side payment rules, the shopping-list discipline and most push items. Many partials keep the job but drop the number or the scene.

How it was pushed
  • BAY317::BP0991 + BAY317::BP0992 (Min's own resale-site pair): 'you don't even have to use venteco.com to buy, use it to sell your stuff' made 'Post your ads' a full seller move.
  • BAY225 + BAY007::BP0083 ('That's kind of what you're looking for, right?') tied 'economical' to the friend's goal: full.
  • BAY330::BP0925 drilled part + BAY296 ('you don't have to go there in person' / 'go whenever you're free') carried 'no trip, no opening hours' for a website: full.
  • BCY039 drilled part 'it's probably around [price] [plan]' with [plan] = 'in a store' gave the $800 new price in full (with 'second-hand' it carries the $250, partial).
  • BCY115 ('don't just take my word for it') marks the worked numbers as an example: full.
  • BAY327::BP0290 with [thing] = 'wood or metal furniture' made the furniture check full.
  • BAY296::BP0711 with [person] = 'you, the seller' plus BAY319 ('you wouldn't have to make yourself available for a ton of people every time') made the single pickup window full.
  • BAY133::BP0755 ('I'd be down to do it with you') answers the tired 'maybe' by offering your time: full.
  • Raised from none to partial only: BCY015 with 'concession automobile' (car dealer alternative), BCY054 (a discount isn't a reason, for the shopping-list rule), BAY483::BP0296 (pricing from similar listings), BCY110::BP0981 (does the site take a cut), BAY480::BP0023 with 'a jewelry store' (floor price for jewelry), BAY481 with 'purchase date' (an appliance's age).

Prompt

You have read this advertisement. You talk about it to a friend who loves cinema very much.

BECOME A FILM CRITIC

Is cinema your passion?

The Academy of Cinema is looking for general-public viewers.

Become a film critic for one year.

Get access to film premieres

Share your ideas with various juries

Get free cinema tickets

Information: www.critique-public-academieducinema.com

Consigne

Vous avez lu cette annonce. Vous en parlez à un(e) ami(e) qui aime beaucoup le cinéma.

DEVENEZ CRITIQUE DE CINÉMA

Le cinéma est votre passion ?

L'Académie Du Cinéma recherche des spectateurs grand public.

Devenez critique de cinéma pendant un an.

Accédez aux avant-premières de films

Partagez vos idées avec différents jurys

Obtenez des places de cinéma gratuites

Renseignements : www.critique-public-academieducinema.com

main line 15/71 full · branches 4/14 full · push further 1/19 full
Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 32 full grades and kept 20; 12 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry the spine of this blueprint: the opener, becoming a critic for one year, seeing films before they open, free cinema tickets on films you pay for anyway, the homework, catch and cost-of-applying answers, and moving to the site. They break in three places. The friend's own evidence (films last year, the one they crossed the city for, tickets last month) has no question cards. The personal offers that make yes easy (I type, I drive, I play the jury) do not exist. Most of 'How far it goes' (rewatching for free, the log, opinions on record) needs cinema-and-opinion cards the bank lacks. Checks survive mostly as 'call them' cards.

How it was pushed
  • BAY215 with [tickets]/[cinema]/[cinema] says "des places de cinéma gratuites", the ad's own words, plus "you already spend money on the cinema": full for the tickets and the homework answer.
  • BAY003::BP0396 with [cinema]/[films]/[premiere] gives "voir des films en avant-première" for "you'd see films before they open".
  • BAY004::BP0407 with [cinema]/[premieres] answers "a year of homework": you already go, you'd keep doing what you love, plus premieres.
  • BAY215::BP0243 drilled part with [see films]: "you'd get to see films for free" for the separate free screenings.
  • BAY251::BP0403 drilled part with [writing]: "no need to be comfortable writing; the ad doesn't mention it", paired with BAY249::BP0858 [a diploma], makes the "only requirement" move full.
  • QB057 from the Section A bank (no vous) asks the monthly figure: [free tickets] for the ticket limit, [screenings] in the close.
  • BAY433::BP0849 [apply]/[the spot] + BAY286 make "applying costs them one evening" full.
  • BCY114::BP0696 drilled part + BCY110::BP0981 cover "you know nothing about this Academy beyond the ad".
  • BAY133 + BCY111 carry "we go together, if guests are allowed" with its condition.
  • BCY115 + BAY483 turn "what's the catch" into "don't take my word for it, let's look at their site".
  • BAY342::BP1184 drilled part with [proofreading] gives "I read the application before it goes".
  • BCY020::BP0706 [be a film critic]/[one year] + BAY292::BP0832 make the one-year, built-in-stop move full.
  • BAY484::BP0104 drilled part with [film programme] makes "check which films are involved before deciding" full.
  • Partial lifts from none: BAY449 for "an Academy can find pros anytime"; BAY100 [premieres]/[films]/[come out] for not waiting for the opening weekend; BAY018 [the blockbusters] for why a big film works; BAY299::BP0317 [tonight] for the backup evening; BAY193 for last month's tickets.

SPORTY WEEKEND

Sporty weekends, tailor-made, adapted to your wishes

Alone, as a couple or among friends

Choose your destination: sea or mountain

kayaking, surfing, diving, boating…

And many other activities to discover!

Contact us at: www.weekends-sportifs.com

Weekends sportifs, sur mesure, adaptés à vos envies

Seul, en couple ou entre amis

Choisissez votre destination : mer ou montagne

Randonnée, snowboard, ski, escalade

kayak, surf, plongée, bateau…

Et bien d’autres activités à découvrir !

How it was pushed
  • BCY023's drilled part ("the exact activities depend on the destination") carries "one destination per weekend, and the choice cuts the list in two" (move 19).
  • BAY336::BP0351 with intensity in its blank turns a trip-pace card into the answer to the slow-group fear (move 47).
  • BAY004::BP0407 (climbing wall, real cliffs) plus BAY263::BP1064 (guides) carries the indoor climber's step to real rock (move 5).
  • BAY480::BP0481 with "plan Bs" in its blank asks for a backup plan for each day (move 74).
  • BAY328::BP0162 ("maybe they even have something on [activity] or [topic]") carries the open-list asks while promising nothing (move 36); BCY110 turns the ad's vaguest line into a question (move 35).
  • CB044 (A bank, no "vous") plus BAY481 with "group discount": the ad doesn't say, so we ask (move 18).
  • A-bank lines with no "vous" (CB018, CB010::C014, QB016::Q021, QB017, QB029::QN18, QB156), dictated while the two of you type the request, carry its items (moves 95-105); QB017 with BCY110::BP0145 also covers "no price, and no word on what's included" (move 66).
  • BAY064 plus BAY468: there are lots of other activities, and the ones you're already comfortable with won't stick, so "to discover" is the pull (move 34).
  • BAY325::BP0590 plus BAY026: pick the sport you like, build the weekend around it, the point is a first time (move 87).
  • BAY298 with "two days" in its blank moves the talk straight to dates (move 89); its drilled part answers "my weekends are taken" (move 69).
  • BAY091 with "challenge" in its blank gives a sporty friend a target (move 51).
  • BAY316's drilled part plus BAY315::BP0998 carry "tailor-made lets you leave the risky one out" (move 79).
  • BAY352 plus BAY263::BP0425: the organizer removes the barriers (move 30).

Audit: an independent reviewer re-checked the builder's 10 full grades and kept 8; 2 came down to partial or gap.

The builder's read, before the audit: Min's cards carry this blueprint's checks, not its scenes. The opening offer, the questions read off the site (area, groceries, allergies, how far ahead to book, the 10%'s small print) and the money-first branch land, often through Section A question cards with no 'vous'. They break on what makes this ad this ad: the host on the sofa at half past eight, guests at the counter, ten plates at once, hosting as everything but the kitchen. No card names food, a kitchen, guests or a bill, so those moves go generic ("they're pros", "a unique experience") or go missing. The co-host offers (pay half, bring drinks) and the close (pick a Saturday, text two dates) have no card.

How it was pushed
  • Area check: QB038::QG001 "Is there a distance limit for [the chef's visit]?" plus BCY105 "if it's super far, forget it" makes 'do they come to you, else it's over' full.
  • Groceries on top: QB016::Q210 "So in that case, how much would it come to, total?" carries the branch whole.
  • Allergy and vegetarian check: QB161 (one of the [guests] with a [food] [allergy]) plus QB144 (how far we could customise the [menu]) took it from none to full.
  • How far ahead to book: QB048 from the A bank replaces a 'call them' card, since the ad gives no phone.
  • Small print of the 10%: QB079::Q201 with [discount] carries 'read the 10% closely'.
  • Money-first branch: CB044::C069 'my first question would be the price, since the ad doesn't say' plus BAY484::BP0773.
  • "Shouldn't the host cook?": BAY449::BP1171 drilled part, "these [guests] aren't coming to your place for a [home-made] [meal]".
  • Tiny kitchen: QB109 "Do you need a particular [kitchen] for this kind of [dinner party]?" and BAY350 with [space] for 'if it won't work, we drop it before anyone is invited'.
  • Washing-up branch: BAY342 drilled part with [messy], "I'll handle all the messy, exhausting stuff".
  • Saturdays fill first: CB047::C075 with [a Saturday] from the A bank.
  • Host gets the experience too: BCY019 drilled part (something you mostly do for others) plus BAY464 (you're allowed to put yourself first).
